Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors: New, severe, continuous headache for 3 days with photophobia and right-eye emphasis; intermittent relief with ibuprofen; not associated with fever; no reported weight change; affects ability to work; no known chronic diseases documented; on combined oral contraceptive pill for about 1 year; alcohol use ~3 drinks per week; non-smoker.
- Family history of chronic conditions: Mother has migraines.
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines: Oral contraceptive pill; ibuprofen; paracetamol as needed; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks: Combined oral contraceptive pill; pregnancy status not documented.
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use: Alcohol ~3 drinks per week; non-smoker; physical activity and diet not recorded.
- Hearing and vision concerns: Vision concerns present (photophobia; transient visual phenomena such as flashes/shooting lights); eye examination recently performed with no changes reported.
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm): Not recorded.
- Social context: Lives alone; works from home; no smoking; supports and housing status not otherwise detailed.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis: Acute migraine-type headache, most likely migraine with aura given photophobia and transient visual phenomena, new onset with significant functional impact.
  - Rationale: Woke with severe headache, constant since onset, right-eye emphasis, photophobia, visual phenomena, family history of migraines, partial response to NSAIDs, no fever or systemic signs; recent use of combined oral contraceptive pill could influence migraine pattern.
- Supporting/explanatory considerations from DDx (consistent with transcript):
  - Primary consideration: Migraine with aura.
  - Secondary headache considerations to monitor for and rule out with exam/imaging as indicated: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) related to estrogen-containing oral contraceptive; idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH); intracranial mass; meningitis/encephalitis (lower likelihood given current features).
- Plan:
  - Diagnostic/assessment actions: Schedule a full neurological examination and fundoscopy; perform BP check during that examination; review need to modify oral contraceptive therapy if migrainous features persist or worsen.
  - Treatments/medication: Provide a stronger NSAID alternative for short-term use (taken with food) plus paracetamol as needed; continue current NSAIDs as advised; no dose/route/frequency documented for these medications.
  - Monitoring and red flags: If headaches worsen, change character, or new neurological symptoms emerge (e.g., weakness, confusion, fever, neck stiffness, visual loss), seek urgent evaluation (A&E).
  - Follow-up: Appointment to be booked via support line for comprehensive examination; if symptoms settle, the visit can be canceled.
  - Contraception considerations: If migrainous features persist, consideration given to changing the oral contraceptive; BP will be checked to ensure continued suitability of therapy.
  - Education: Advise taking medications with food; reassess if headaches persist or progress; seek urgent care if red-flag symptoms develop.
- Conflict noted: Not identified between transcript and DDx.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification: Education on red flags requiring urgent evaluation and migraine management strategies; medication safety (take with food); monitor for changes in headache pattern or new neurological signs.
- Patient health goals and priorities: Not explicitly recorded.
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA): Not recorded.
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports): Referral to be arranged via support line for full examination; potential referrals to neurology or ophthalmology if indicated by exam findings.
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled: Follow-up to include a full neurological examination and fundoscopy; status reviewed after appointment; ability to cancel if symptoms resolve.

- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management: Consider neurology referral if headaches persist or worsen.
- Dental referral: Not recorded.
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening: Consider if visual symptoms persist or change; fundoscopy planned.
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected: Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Migraine with aura (Migraine-type headache)
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Photophobia, visual phenomena (flashes), unilateral/right-eye emphasis, new severe headache with functional impairment, family history of migraines, partial NSAID response; no fever or systemic signs.
- Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) related to estrogen-containing oral contraceptive
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: New, persistent headache in a woman on estrogen-containing OCP; risk factor present; morning-predominant headaches can occur; requires imaging to confirm.
- Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri)
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Female on the younger side of this age range with headaches and visual symptoms; IIH can present with morning headaches and photophobia; fundoscopy would help identify papilledema.
- Intracranial mass or raised intracranial pressure from a lesion
  - Likelihood: Low
  - Justification: Persistent headache with right-eye emphasis could occur with intracranial mass; onset over 3 days is plausible but less typical without focal neuro signs.
- Meningitis/encephalitis (infectious/inflammatory)
  - Likelihood: Low
  - Justification: Photophobia and headache can occur; absence of fever, meningismus, altered mental status, or systemic signs lowers likelihood.

Quality checks

- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs not recorded; immunisation status not documented; no objective activity/diet data; no explicit BP measurement at this visit.
- Internal conflicts or contradictions between transcript and DDx: None identified; DDx aligns with migraine as primary consideration and flags secondary diagnoses to monitor due to OCP use.
- Transcript quality notes: Initial audio issues with hearing during the call (documented in transcript) but subsequent communication completed; exam plan and ophthalmic considerations were clearly discussed.

End of note.
